deep.reconstruction:
Context (previous page and this one): this is the draft of Riemann's 1857 note 'Zwei allgemeine Saetze ueber lineare Differentialgleichungen mit algebraischen Coefficienten', printed posthumously in the Werke (1876, No. XXI). The objects are a system (y) = (y_1,...,y_n) of multivalued functions of x. They have branch points a,b,...,g and given monodromy substitutions (A),(B),...,(G). At each branch point there is a canonical basis (A)^{-1}(y), in which y_i ~ (x-a)^{alpha_i}·(holomorphic); the alpha_i are the exponents. The 'characteristic' is the set of substitutions together with the exponents.

(1) Lowering the freedom by raising exponents. The previous page shows that every system (Y) with the same substitutions, exponents not lower than those of (y), and no other singularities, has the form Y_i = k y_i + k_1 y_i' + ... + k_m y_i^{(m)}. Here the k_j are (after normalisation) constants. Riemann now fixes one constant after another as a function of the remaining ones. Each choice makes the leading coefficient of one component of some canonical expansion (A)^{-1}(Y), ..., (G)^{-1}(Y) vanish. Each such step raises the exponent sum by at least 1 and removes one free constant.
- Riemann first wrote 'and, as can be proved, also only by one unit'. He struck this and inserted 'wenigstens' (at least) in the margin.
- After the process the exponent sum has been raised by at least the number of constants eliminated. That number is m on the reading below (the transcription has n).
- Only one free constant remains: a factor common to all functions.
- Result: from any system of n functions one derives a system with higher exponents. This new system is determined by its characteristic (substitutions plus exponents) up to a common constant factor.

(2) Normalisation. The common factor is fixed by setting the coefficient of the lowest power of (x-a) in the expansion of the first component of (A)^{-1}(y) equal to 1. Now y is uniquely determined by its characteristic.

(3) Dependence on a branch point (the main claim). Let the branch point a move while all substitutions (A),...,(G) stay fixed. Riemann asserts that the uniquely normalised y_i, regarded as functions of a, again form a system of the same kind:
- its branch points (in the a-plane) are b, c, ..., g, x;
- its substitutions are composed from (A),...,(G).
In modern terms, y(x; a, b, ..., g) is an isomonodromic family. Its monodromy in the deformation parameters comes from braiding a around the other singular points.

(4) Degenerate case. It may be impossible to vary a while keeping all substitutions constant. This happens when there are fewer free constants than conditions to satisfy. Riemann then treats the system as a special case of a system with lower exponents: for these special values of a,...,g, the leading coefficients of some series in the canonical expansions vanish. This is continued on the next page.

The next page draws the conclusion. The y_i are functions of p variables a,...,g,x which return to linear combinations of themselves, with constant coefficient systems built from the given (A),...,(F), when the variables go around closed paths. Riemann adds that abelian integrals are a special case and lead to general theta functions.
errors: The deleted clause ('and, as can be proved, only by one unit') was rightly withdrawn. A single vanishing condition on a leading coefficient can raise the exponent sum by more than 1, since lower coefficients may vanish simultaneously. Riemann's correction to 'wenigstens' (at least) is the accurate statement.

Count of eliminated constants: the family has m+1 constants k,...,k_m, and reducing to one common factor removes m of them. So the exponent sum rises by at least m, not n. The transcription's 'n' is probably a misreading of 'm'. If Riemann really wrote n, it is a slip.

The main claim (3) is asserted, not proved ('man hat nur noethig scharf aufzufassen'). Analytic dependence on a, existence of the deformation, and the treatment of non-generic or resonant exponents are not justified here. This gap was filled only by later work (Fuchs, Schlesinger, Garnier).
Point (4) presupposes that constant-count arguments (number of constants versus number of conditions) suffice. That is heuristic, in the style of Riemann's constant counts.

results.what: Systems with prescribed monodromy and exponent bounds form the family k y + k_1 y' + ... + k_m y^{(m)}. Imposing vanishing of leading coefficients raises exponents and leaves a system unique up to a constant factor (normalised to 1).
results.modern_name: Uniqueness of a Fuchsian system or equation from its monodromy and local exponents up to scalar (rigidity-type and Schlesinger-transformation-type argument)
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann 1857 (published in Werke 1876); later Fuchs, Schlesinger

results.what: Normalised solutions, as functions of a branch point a with monodromy held fixed, form a system of the same type with branch points b,...,g,x and substitutions composed of (A),...,(G).
results.modern_name: Isomonodromic deformation (Schlesinger and Garnier systems, Painleve VI); Hurwitz-braid action on monodromy

results.what: Degenerate case: when constant counting prevents isomonodromic variation, view the system as a specialisation of one with lower exponents in which leading coefficients vanish.
results.modern_name: Apparent singularities / Schlesinger transformations shifting exponents by integers

deep.surprise_reason: The page is the draft of the 1857 fragment printed in Riemann's Werke (No. XXI). Historians (e.g. Gray, Its, Bolibruch-style surveys) already credit Riemann with this anticipation of isomonodromic deformations. The draft adds only minor details: the struck 'only by one unit' claim and the inserted 'wenigstens'.

checkable.sympy: x,a,b,al,be=symbols('x a b alpha beta'); y=(x-a)**al*(x-b)**be; simplify(diff(y,a)+al*y/(x-a))==0
checkable.asserts: Rank-one isomonodromic example: y=(x-a)^alpha (x-b)^beta depends on a with constant monodromy, and dy/da = -alpha*y/(x-a). As a function of a, y is branched at a=x.

Differentiation lowers the local exponent at a by one. So in Y = k y + k1 y' + ..., the derivative terms carry lower exponents, which is why vanishing conditions on leading coefficients are needed to keep or raise the exponents.

checkable.sympy: t,c0,c1,c2,al=symbols('t c0 c1 c2 alpha'); f=t**al*(c0+c1*t+c2*t**2); series(f.subs(c0,0).subs(c1,0)/t**al,t,0,3)
checkable.asserts: Setting one leading coefficient to zero can raise the exponent by more than one when the next coefficient also vanishes. This supports deleting the claim 'only by one unit' and inserting 'at least'.

transcription_corrections: 'die Exponentensumme um {+wenigstens+} n erhoeht': the symbol is more plausibly 'm', matching k_1..k_m on the previous page. 'wenigstens' is a marginal insertion shown on the right ('|wenigstens|').
'Anzahl der willkuerlichen Constanten in den Functionen y' should probably read 'Functionen Y', the derived system.
'der ersten von den Functionen (A)^{-1}(y)': the image is consistent with (A)^{-1}(y) for the final normalised system, so this is fine.

The struck passage reads '[und, wie sich beweisen laesst, auch nur um eine Einheit vermindert wird]'. The underlined 'vermindert' (wavy and dotted) suggests the intended word was 'erhoeht' in relation to the exponent sum. The whole clause is deleted.
